title: MongoDB Quiz
description: Review the ideas from the lessons. Take your time. After each answer, read the note that explains the rule. You can try again.

questions.question: What is one record called in MongoDB?
questions.explanation: A document keeps named values together. A book document could have title and pages fields.

questions.question: A group of MongoDB documents is called a ___.
questions.explanation: A collection groups documents, just as a shelf groups books. A database can have several collections.

questions.question: What does a connection string tell a database tool?
questions.explanation: A connection string is like an address for a database. Keep a real connection string private if it includes a password.
options: How many lines a lesson has
Where the database is and how to connect
Which colour to paint the page

questions.question: On a new empty collection, what number is printed after these commands in mongosh?
questions.explanation: insertOne adds one document. pages is just a field value; it does not add extra documents.

questions.question: What does findOne return when nothing matches?
questions.explanation: findOne gives one matching document, or null if none matches. find gives a cursor you can read through.

questions.question: Why is this not the right filter for pages greater than 20?
questions.explanation: MongoDB query operators start with $. Write { pages: { $gt: 20 } } for greater than 20.
options: The collection must have only one book

questions.question: Fill the gap to find red or blue books: { colour: { ___: ["red", "blue"] } }.
questions.explanation: $in matches any value in the list. It is useful when several answers are allowed.

questions.question: Assume lessonScores starts empty. What score is printed in mongosh?
questions.explanation: $inc adds to a number that is already there. Three plus two is five.

questions.question: What is wrong with this updateOne command?
questions.explanation: Use { $set: { pages: 30 } } to change one field. Use replaceOne when you want to replace a whole document.
options: The change needs an update operator such as $set
The title cannot contain a space

questions.question: A book has three short notes that are always read with it. What is a simple way to store them?
questions.explanation: Small related values that are read together can fit in one document. Very large or shared lists may need separate documents.
options: In a different database for every word
As a small array inside the book document

questions.question: In $lookup, the field in the current collection is named ___.
questions.explanation: localField names the current-side field. foreignField names the matching field in the other collection.

questions.question: An index is { name: 1, score: 1 }. Which field is its first, or prefix, field?
questions.explanation: The field order matters. This index starts with name, so searches by name can use that first part.

questions.question: lessonFruit contains three documents: apple, apple, pear. How many groups does this pipeline produce?
questions.explanation: There are two different names. Both apple documents go into one group; pear goes into the other.

questions.question: Which deployment supports MongoDB transactions?
questions.explanation: A transaction groups changes into one all-or-nothing job. MongoDB needs a replica set or sharded cluster for it.
options: A replica set or a sharded cluster
Any standalone server with no replica set

questions.question: A tool only needs to read books. Which role should it get?
questions.explanation: Give a tool only the access it needs. A read-only tool does not need permission to delete documents.
options: A shared password printed on the page
A read-only role for the needed database
An admin role for every database
